studies.label: Field experiment: ChatGPT access in a Chinese technology consulting firm
studies.cluster_se_treatment: People were individually randomized, not supervisors or departments. The paper uses employee-level multilevel analyses with nesting within supervisors and departments (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Results); Table 2 instead reports independent-samples t tests (same page, footnote 2).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Participants and Procedure; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), continuation of assignment procedure and Results; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 6), Table 1 note
counts_source.quote:
Due to business travel and illnesses, 36 employees did not participate, resulting in a ﬁnal sample of 250 employees.
N = 250.

arms.name: LLM assistance
arms.description: Employees received personal ChatGPT accounts through the firm’s API-based interface and usage examples, with instructions not to share accounts or discuss them with others. Workplace usage was confirmed by self-reports and account logs (PDF pp. 5–6, printed pp. 4–5, Method).

arms.name: Control (no LLM assistance)
arms.description: No LLM assistance; no control employee reported ChatGPT use (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

studies.task: Employees generated detailed written suggestions for protecting employee privacy when companies use digital devices, in an endpoint survey following assignment to ChatGPT workplace access or no LLM assistance.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT through the firm’s OpenAI API-based interface; underlying model version not stated
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), Introduction: "In November 2022, OpenAI launched ChatGPT"; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Empirical Setting, and PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Participants and Procedure. Year is the stated product launch year, not a confirmed underlying-model version.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Transparency and Openness: "This study is not preregistered."

estimates.outcome: Novelty of the written privacy-protection response (external raters; unadjusted ttest)
estimates.measure_detail: Two external human raters independently evaluated novelty using the consensual assessment technique, on a scale from 1 (least) to 5 (most). Their qualifications and the method of combining their scores are not stated (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Dependent Variable: Creativity). The measure code is null because neither lay/crowd nor expert status is established.

estimates.notes: AI availability while composing the privacy-protection response is not stated: the methods report workplace account use and an endpoint survey, but no task-specific AI-use instructions or removal of access. Following the reconciled form and the instruction not to guess, question and outcome_with_ai remain null. The numeric evidence is retained provisionally; with_ai versus after_ai classification must be settled before question-specific inclusion. The survey is an intervention-endpoint measure, not a documented later retention test. Table 2 gives unadjusted arm means, SDs, independent-samples t-test p values, and Cohen’s d. It prints no arm counts, t statistic, degrees of freedom, or definition of the d standardizer; these are not inferred. SDs and the test concern employee-level response scores, not independent rater observations. Table 2 source quotes select the two cells under the named outcome, in control then LLM order. Arm standard errors shown only as unlabeled error bars in Figure 2 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 8) are not read from the figure. Adjusted Table 3 models are excluded because controls include postassignment measures.

regression.model: Multilevel usefulness regression without control variables. Results describe employees nested within supervisors nested within departments; the coefficient is attributed in the main text to Supplemental Table S5 Model 4. Footnote 2 instead refers to Supplemental Materials S4. The separate supplement was unavailable, so its internal locator and full specification are not verified. No robust or cluster-robust SE estimator is named.

estimates.notes: AI availability while composing the privacy-protection response is not stated: the methods report workplace account use and an endpoint survey, but no task-specific AI-use instructions or removal of access. Following the reconciled form and the instruction not to guess, question and outcome_with_ai remain null. The numeric evidence is retained provisionally; with_ai versus after_ai classification must be settled before question-specific inclusion. The survey is an intervention-endpoint measure, not a documented later retention test. This full-sample coefficient without controls is printed directly in the main PDF and is retained despite the unavailable supplement. It is not the post-treatment-adjusted Table 3 coefficient. The model operates on one response score per individually randomized employee and accounts for the organizational hierarchy, so se_basis is participant; supervisors and departments were not randomization units. SE estimator details are not stated. This is an alternative analysis of the same usefulness contrast already represented by the Table 2 record, not another independent estimate for pooling. Arm descriptives and Cohen’s d are in that companion record and are not presented here as multilevel fitted means or model-standardized effects.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Creativity (supervisor rating), including unadjusted and adjusted comparisons
not_extracted.reason: Supervisors rated employees’ general creative performance over the week, not an identified participant-produced output. This fails the output-scoring requirement (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Dependent Variable: Creativity; Tables 2 and 3 on PDF pp. 8 and 10, printed pp. 7 and 9).

not_extracted.what: Cognitive job resources, including the overall scale and item-level analyses
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported work resources and a mediator, not creativity scored on produced output (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Mediator and Moderator; PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, Exploratory Analyses and Robustness Tests).
Self-reported moderator, not an output-based creativity or diversity measure (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Mediator and Moderator).

not_extracted.what: Creative self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation, job insecurity, and heuristic-task-characteristic measures
not_extracted.reason: Attitudinal, motivational, and job-characteristic control measures rather than scored creative output. Attitudinal and motivational measures were collected after assignment in the second survey (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Participants and Procedure and Controls).

not_extracted.what: ChatGPT usage and usage-frequency reports and account logs
not_extracted.reason: Manipulation and compliance checks, not creativity or diversity scored on output (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Adjusted novelty effects in Table 3 Models 3, 6, and 10
not_extracted.reason: These models adjust for postassignment attitudinal/motivational variables; the latter models also include a post-treatment mediator and, for the interaction model, moderation terms. They do not meet the extraction rule excluding effects adjusted for post-treatment variables (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Participants and Procedure and Controls; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3). The unadjusted Table 2 contrast is retained.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: Adjusted usefulness effects in Table 3 Models 4, 7, and 11
not_extracted.reason: These models adjust for postassignment attitudinal/motivational variables; the latter models also include a post-treatment mediator and, for the interaction model, moderation terms. They are excluded under the post-treatment-adjustment rule (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Participants and Procedure and Controls; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3). Both available no-controls analyses are retained separately.

not_extracted.what: Mediation and moderated-mediation effects for creativity, novelty, and usefulness
not_extracted.reason: Indirect and conditional indirect effects through cognitive job resources, rather than eligible full-sample randomized-arm total effects (PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, H3 and H5 results; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3).

not_extracted.what: Interactions, simple slopes, conditional effects, and regions of significance involving metacognitive strategies
not_extracted.reason: Moderation and conditional/subgroup analyses are outside extraction scope (PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, H4 and H5; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Figures 3 and 4).

not_extracted.what: Additional no-controls multilevel novelty statistics referenced only in the unavailable supplement
not_extracted.reason: The main-text footnote describes consistent effects but does not provide an outcome-specific novelty coefficient, SE, or exact p value for the no-controls multilevel model. No values are inferred from its range of p values or substituted from the ineligible adjusted model. The full-sample novelty contrast is already retained from Table 2 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, footnote 2; PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, Table 2).

open_items: AI availability during the privacy-protection writing task remains unresolved for S1-O2 and S1-O3. Confirm task instructions or account-access records before assigning with_ai versus after_ai. The three numerical records intentionally retain null question and outcome_with_ai; they must not enter a question-specific synthesis until resolved.

Arm-specific randomized and analyzed participant counts are not printed. Total sample size is confirmed, but a balanced split must not be derived from the rounded treatment-indicator mean or other statistics.
The external raters are human, but neither lay/crowd-worker status nor domain expertise is stated. Confirm their qualifications to code human_raters versus expert_raters; measure remains null.

The separate supplement at https://doi.org/10.1037/apl0001296.supp was not accessible. It may provide additional unadjusted multilevel statistics and clarify the inconsistent S5 Model 4 versus S4 references, as well as details of the model and SE estimator.

The paper does not define the standardizer used for its reported Cohen’s d values or state exactly how the external raters’ scores were combined. Participant-level arm SDs are printed, but participant counts by arm are missing.
Figure 2 shows arm SE error bars without numeric labels; no SE values are transcribed from their geometry.
notes: Read the complete markdown conversion from beginning to end, including all references and end matter; the saved PDF has no appended supplement or embedded attachment. Checked the cited PDF pages using PyMuPDF text extraction. The rotated Table 2 is scrambled in markdown; its complete PDF text was checked for column order and all recorded cells. No effect sizes, SEs, differences, arm counts, or intervals were computed. n_randomized uses the final sample described before the subsequent random-assignment step; n_analyzed is confirmed by the analysis text and Table 1 note. No postassignment exclusions are reported. The qualifying written task is coded idea_generation rather than the screening form’s broader other category for general workplace duties. Three numerical records cover two output outcomes in one sample; the usefulness t-test and multilevel results must not be counted as independent evidence. They remain provisionally unclassified because task-specific AI availability is not established. This deliberate use of null categorical values follows the user’s instruction not to guess and the reconciled form’s unresolved fields. No shared sample with another paper is stated; shared_sample is null rather than a claim of proven independence. No across-person diversity outcome or documented later AI-removal assessment is reported; the discussion of possible long-term dependence is explicitly future research (PDF pp. 11–12, printed pp. 10–11). The supplement was sought locally and via Python urllib requests using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to its DOI and then the named Crossref fallback https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037%2Fapl0001296.supp; both requests failed with socket-access-denied errors. Only the main document was used. Data and materials are available on request but cannot be publicly shared because of a confidentiality agreement (PDF p. 5, printed p. 4, Transparency and Openness).
